points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 查理曼于747年左右在法兰克王国的埃克斯-拉-夏佩勒（今德国亚琛）附近出生，是丕平三世的次子。他的童年主要在法兰克王国的宫廷中度过，接受了当时最好的教育，包括拉丁语、希腊语和日耳曼语的学习。768年，父亲丕平三世去世，查理曼与他的兄弟卡洛曼共同继承法兰克王国，但两人关系紧张，为日后的权力斗争埋下伏笔。这段时期塑造了查理曼的军事才能和政治智慧，为他日后统一法兰克王国奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Charlemagne was born around 747 near Aachen (now Germany) in the Frankish Kingdom, as the second son of Pepin III. His childhood was spent in the Frankish court, receiving the best education available, including Latin, Greek, and German languages. In 768, after his father's death, Charlemagne shared the Frankish Kingdom with his brother Carloman, though their relationship was tense, laying the groundwork for future power struggles. This period shaped Charlemagne's military abilities and political wisdom, laying the foundation for his later unification of the Frankish Kingdom.

points.title: 共治时期
points.description: 768年，查理曼与兄弟卡洛曼共同继承法兰克王国，以塞纳河为界分治。查理曼统治王国的北部和东部，包括纽斯特里亚、奥斯特拉西亚和阿基坦地区。这一时期，查理曼开始展现其军事才能，成功镇压了阿基坦的叛乱。771年，卡洛曼突然去世，查理曼成为法兰克王国的唯一统治者，结束了短暂的共治时期。巴黎作为法兰克王国的政治中心，见证了查理曼如何通过军事和政治手段巩固自己的权力，为日后的扩张做准备。
points.descriptionEn: In 768, Charlemagne shared the Frankish Kingdom with his brother Carloman, dividing it along the Seine River. Charlemagne ruled the northern and eastern parts, including Neustria, Austrasia, and Aquitaine. During this period, Charlemagne began demonstrating his military capabilities by successfully suppressing a rebellion in Aquitaine. In 771, Carloman suddenly died, making Charlemagne the sole ruler of the Frankish Kingdom and ending the brief co-reign period. Paris, as the political center of the Frankish Kingdom, witnessed how Charlemagne consolidated his power through military and political means, preparing for future expansion.

points.title: 征服意大利
points.description: 成为法兰克王国唯一统治者后，查理曼开始大规模扩张。773-774年，他率领军队翻越阿尔卑斯山，征服了伦巴第王国，将意大利北部并入法兰克王国。778年，他远征西班牙，但遭遇了著名的龙塞斯瓦列斯战役的失败。795年，他派兵征服了巴伐利亚，结束了该地区的独立地位。799年，教皇利奥三世遭到罗马贵族的攻击，向查理曼求援。查理曼率军进入罗马，恢复了教皇的地位。这一系列军事行动不仅大大扩展了法兰克王国的疆域，也使查理曼成为基督教世界的保护者，为800年的加冕奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After becoming the sole ruler of the Frankish Kingdom, Charlemagne began large-scale expansion. From 773-774, he led his army across the Alps, conquered the Lombard Kingdom, and incorporated northern Italy into the Frankish realm. In 778, he launched an expedition to Spain but suffered the famous defeat at the Battle of Roncesvalles. In 795, he sent troops to conquer Bavaria, ending the region's independence. In 799, Pope Leo III was attacked by Roman nobles and sought Charlemagne's help. Charlemagne entered Rome, restored the pope's position. These military actions not only significantly expanded the Frankish Kingdom's territory but also established Charlemagne as the protector of the Christian world, laying the foundation for his coronation in 800.

points.title: 神圣罗马皇帝
points.description: 800年圣诞节，查理曼在罗马圣彼得大教堂由教皇利奥三世加冕为'罗马人的皇帝'，这一事件标志着西罗马帝国灭亡后西方世界皇帝头衔的恢复。查理曼最初对这一加冕感到意外，但很快接受了这一称号，并开始以皇帝身份统治。他建立了以亚琛为中心的帝国行政体系，推行卡洛曼改革，加强中央集权。他重视教育，建立了宫廷学校，邀请欧洲各地的学者到亚琛。他还颁布了大量法律，统一了度量衡和货币。作为皇帝，查理曼致力于维护基督教世界的统一，多次与拜占庭帝国和阿拉伯帝国进行外交接触，试图建立欧洲的和平与秩序。
points.descriptionEn: On Christmas Day 800, Charlemagne was crowned 'Emperor of the Romans' by Pope Leo III in St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. This event marked the restoration of the imperial title in the Western world after the fall of the Western Roman Empire. Although initially surprised by the coronation, Charlemagne quickly accepted the title and began ruling as emperor. He established an imperial administrative system centered in Aachen, implemented the Carolingian Reforms to strengthen central authority. He emphasized education, establishing a palace school and inviting scholars from across Europe to Aachen. He also issued numerous laws, standardizing weights, measures, and currency. As emperor, Charlemagne was committed to maintaining unity in the Christian world, engaging in diplomatic contacts with the Byzantine and Arab Empires in an attempt to establish European peace and order.

points.title: 逝世与遗产
points.description: 814年1月28日，查理曼在亚琛的宫殿中因肺炎去世，享年约67岁。他被安葬在亚琛大教堂，其陵墓至今保存完好。查理曼的去世标志着他建立的庞大帝国的开始瓦解，他的三个儿子瓜分了帝国。然而，查理曼的遗产远远超出了他的帝国疆域。他推动了欧洲的文化复兴，被称为'卡洛曼文艺复兴'，为后来的中世纪欧洲奠定了基础。他建立的行政体系、法律和教育制度影响了欧洲数百年。他的加冕事件被视为中世纪欧洲神圣罗马帝国的开端，影响了欧洲的政治格局近千年。查理曼被后世誉为'欧洲之父'，他的形象成为欧洲统一和基督教文明的象征。
points.descriptionEn: On January 28, 814, Charlemagne died of pneumonia in his palace in Aachen at approximately 67 years old. He was buried in Aachen Cathedral, where his tomb remains intact to this day. Charlemagne's death marked the beginning of the disintegration of his vast empire, which was divided among his three sons. However, Charlemagne's legacy extends far beyond his imperial borders. He promoted a cultural revival in Europe, known as the 'Carolingian Renaissance,' laying the foundation for later medieval Europe. The administrative system, laws, and educational institutions he established influenced Europe for centuries. His coronation event is considered the beginning of the Holy Roman Empire in the Middle Ages, influencing European political格局 for nearly a millennium. Charlemagne is later hailed as the 'Father of Europe,' his image becoming a symbol of European unity and Christian civilization.

supporter.zh: 查理曼被支持者视为欧洲的伟大统一者和文明复兴的推动者。他通过军事征服和政治智慧，将分裂的西欧大部分地区统一在一个政权之下，结束了长期的混乱局面。他重视教育和文化，推动了卡洛曼文艺复兴，保存了古典知识，为中世纪欧洲的文化发展奠定了基础。他保护基督教，加强与教皇的关系，被视为基督教世界的捍卫者。查理曼建立的行政和法律体系为欧洲中世纪的政治制度提供了模板，他的遗产至今影响着欧洲的统一理念。
supporter.en: Supporters view Charlemagne as a great unifier of Europe and a promoter of civilizational revival. Through military conquest and political wisdom, he unified most of Western Europe under one rule, ending a long period of chaos. He valued education and culture, promoting the Carolingian Renaissance, preserving classical knowledge, and laying the foundation for medieval European cultural development. He protected Christianity and strengthened relations with the papacy, seen as a defender of the Christian world. The administrative and legal systems he established provided a template for medieval European political institutions, and his legacy continues to influence European ideals of unity.

critic.zh: 批评者指出查理曼的统治充满了暴力和强制。他的军事征服导致大量人口死亡和流离失所，如对萨克森人的长达三十年的战争，以强迫改信基督教为名进行残酷镇压。他的行政改革虽然加强了中央集权，但也削弱了地方传统和自治权。查理曼的加冕事件被批评为教皇与世俗权力勾结的产物，为后来教权与皇权的冲突埋下伏笔。此外，他建立的帝国在他死后迅速分裂，表明其统治缺乏持久的基础和合法性。
critic.en: Critics point out that Charlemagne's rule was filled with violence and coercion. His military conquests resulted in numerous deaths and displacements, such as the thirty-year war against the Saxons, which involved brutal suppression under the pretext of forced conversion to Christianity. While his administrative reforms strengthened central authority, they also weakened local traditions and autonomy. His coronation is criticized as a product of collusion between papal and secular powers, sowing the seeds for future conflicts between religious and temporal authority. Additionally, the empire he founded rapidly disintegrated after his death, indicating that his rule lacked lasting foundations and legitimacy.

objective.zh: 从历史学角度看，查理曼是中世纪早期最具影响力的统治者之一，他的统治标志着古代向中世纪的过渡。他既保留了罗马帝国的某些传统，又融入了日耳曼人的统治方式，创造了独特的卡洛曼文明。在流行文化中，查理曼常被理想化为骑士精神和基督教美德的典范，成为欧洲统一和文艺复兴的象征。历史学家普遍认为，查理曼的统治既有建设性的一面，也有暴力扩张的一面，他的遗产是复杂而多面的，反映了中世纪欧洲社会的矛盾与转型。
objective.en: From a historical perspective, Charlemagne was one of the most influential rulers of the early Middle Ages, his reign marking the transition from antiquity to the medieval period. He preserved certain traditions of the Roman Empire while incorporating Germanic methods of rule, creating a unique Carolingian civilization. In popular culture, Charlemagne is often idealized as a paragon of chivalry and Christian virtue, becoming a symbol of European unity and the Renaissance. Historians generally agree that Charlemagne's rule had both constructive and expansionist-violent aspects, and his legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting the contradictions and transformations of medieval European society.

self.zh: 为了上帝的荣耀和基督教的救赎，我努力工作，日夜不辍。
self.en: For the sake of God's glory and the salvation of Christianity, I have labored without ceasing, day and night.

others.zh: 查理曼的统治如此伟大，以至于他几乎可以被称为欧洲的第二个创始人。
others.en: Charlemagne's rule was so great that he might almost be called a second founder of Europe.
